title: Script call-record growth
summary: Recover 0x4f4fd0..0x4f501c as a thiscall member: signed capacity check against 20000, status 5 for already oversized capacity, otherwise wraparound doubling through accepted resize, post-resize signed overflow check and runtime error with stack overflow literal, then reload and advance current by 24 bytes with EAX return. Direct original disassembly and two callers establish layout and return use. External helper integration seams retain dependencies without expanding recovered scope.
test_description: 480 differential cases against original grow with accepted resize, reallocate and throw-status helpers. Capacities include zero, normal sizes, largest nonoverflowing doubled capacity, already oversized positive signed values and selected negative signed values whose doubled counts are safe. Offsets cover alignment, negative differences, signed extremes and address wrap. Controlled allocator tests current mutation, success, null return and zero-size null return. Check EAX, all 112 state bytes, all global bytes, allocator arguments, invocation count, status and allocation accounting.
known_limits: Post-resize overflow path (initial positive capacities 10001..20000) is preserved but not executed: runtime error at 0x486ab0 requires VM formatter 0x4efb10, location and error-dispatch machinery and original data. Test runtime_error seam must never be reached.
Malformed negative capacities that double to oversized allocation requests are not executed; accepted allocation-too-large invokes the same VM error dependency.
Protected longjmp and panic-handler paths are untested; fixtures use null error frame and null panic, allowing original error helpers to return.
32-bit VM address words preserve original wraparound; a native 64-bit port needs address/layout integration. Dependency seams need binding to ported helpers.
No byte-matching claim; native compiler compatibility does not establish matching code generation.
